CUSTOMER TERMS AND CONDITIONS Opulence Bliss Ltd | Version 1.0 | Effective from: 1 October 2026 These terms are for households that book cleaning through our platform. Businesses sign a separate written agreement.

1. About us and these terms

1.1 These terms apply between Opulence Bliss Ltd ("we", "us", "our") and the person who books our services ("you"). Please read them before you book.

1.2 Our details: Opulence Bliss Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales, company number

15894675. Registered office: 128 City Road, London, United Kingdom, EC1V 2NX.

Registered with the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) under number ZC264981. Contact: hello@opulencebliss.com.

1.3 In these terms:

• Booking means a cleaning visit that you book through our platform.

• Cleaner means the self-employed professional who carries out your Booking.

• Standard Cleaning means regular household cleaning.

• Deep Cleaning means deep cleaning and end of tenancy cleaning.

• Products Add-on means the optional service described in clause 5.

• Booking Credit means credit applied to a later Booking, as set out in clause 13.

1.4 You must be at least 18 years old and be booking for a home. When you book, we send you a confirmation by email and a contract is formed between us for that Booking. We recommend that you keep a copy of these terms.

2. Our service

2.1 We provide cleaning services at your home. We use self-employed Cleaners to carry out the work. We are responsible to you for the service under this contract.

2.2 Before a Cleaner takes bookings, we check their identity and right to work, require each Cleaner to hold a basic Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check and show us the certificate, and ask for proof of their own public liability insurance. We also hold public liability insurance for our business.

2.3 We will provide the service with reasonable care and skill and in line with what we described to you when you booked.

2.4 Before you book, we will tell you what is included in Standard Cleaning and Deep Cleaning. If you want anything extra, tell us when you book.

2.5 We do not clean areas that are unsafe or unsanitary, biohazards or human or animal waste, areas that need specialist equipment or cannot be reached safely, or anything that would put a Cleaner at risk. The Cleaner can decline any task they believe is unsafe.

3. Booking

3.1 You book through our platform. The minimum Booking is 2 hours.

3.2 You must give us accurate information about your home, including access, parking, pets, and anything that could affect the clean or a Cleaner's safety.

3.3 We will tell you who your Cleaner is. If your Cleaner cannot attend, we will offer the Booking to another Cleaner and tell you before the visit. You may choose to cancel instead, at no charge.

3.4 Where possible, we will send the same Cleaner to your regular Bookings, but we cannot guarantee this.

3.5 Our guarantee, our insurance, your loyalty rewards and any referral rewards apply only to Bookings made through our platform. They do not apply if you arrange cleaning directly with a Cleaner outside the platform.

4. Prices and payment

4.1 The price shown when you book is the total price you will pay, including every mandatory charge. Our current prices are:

• Standard Cleaning (regular): £18.99 per hour

• Standard Cleaning (one-off): £22.99 per hour

• Deep Cleaning: £25.99 per hour

• Products Add-on (optional): £5 per Booking

4.2 We are not registered for VAT, so no VAT is added to our prices.

4.3 We take payment by card through our payment provider, Stripe. Payment is taken when you book. If you cancel in line with these terms, or we cancel, we will refund what you are owed within 14 days.

4.4 If the Cleaner thinks the job needs more time, they may offer you extra hours. They will only be added if you agree, at the same hourly price. You will not be charged for extra time you have not agreed to.

4.5 If a payment fails, we will tell you and may ask you to pay another way before the Booking goes ahead.

5. Cleaning products

5.1 Unless you choose the Products Add-on, you provide the cleaning products and equipment for your Booking, or tell us in advance if the Cleaner should use yours.

5.2 If you choose the Products Add-on, the Cleaner brings suitable cleaning products for your Booking. You pay £5 per Booking, not per hour.

5.3 Please tell us about any allergies, sensitivities or surfaces that need special care. If you asked for products and your Cleaner does not bring them, we will refund the £5.

6. Tips

6.1 Tipping is optional and does not change the price of your Booking.

6.2100% of your tip goes to your Cleaner. We do not take any part of it.

6.3 Once a tip has been sent to the Cleaner, we cannot usually take it back, unless you sent it by mistake and tell us promptly.

7. Your right to cancel within 14 days

7.1 Under the Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013, you have the right to cancel a Booking within 14 days of the date we confirm it, without giving a reason.

7.2 If you want a Booking to take place within that 14-day period, you must ask us to start the service when you book. If you then cancel after the service has started, you must pay for the part already provided, in proportion to the whole Booking.

7.3 If the Booking has been fully carried out within the 14 days with your express request, you can no longer cancel it.

7.4 To cancel, email hello@opulencebliss.com saying clearly that you want to cancel. We will refund any payment you have made within 14 days of receiving your notice.

7.5 This clause is about your legal right to cancel in the first 14 days. If you are outside this period, clause 8 applies.

8. Changing or cancelling a Booking

8.1 If you cancel a Booking, what we refund depends on how much notice you give before it starts:

• 48 hours or more: full refund

• 24 to 48 hours: 75% refund (25% charged)

• 12 to 24 hours: 50% refund (50% charged)

• Less than 12 hours, or on the day of the visit: no refund

8.2 We encourage you to reschedule a Booking rather than cancel it, and we encourage our Cleaners to do the same.

8.3 The percentage applies to the total you paid for the Booking, not including any tip. We charge only the amount shown above and no other fee. The charge reflects the time your Cleaner kept free for you.

8.4 If the Cleaner cannot get in, or no one is available to let them in, they will wait for 15 minutes and contact you. If they still cannot start, no refund is due.

8.5 If we cancel a Booking for any reason, we will refund you in full and offer you another time.

8.6 If something unavoidable happens, such as illness or an emergency, please tell us. We will consider each case fairly, and we will not charge you where it would be unreasonable to do so.

8.7 If a Cleaner leaves because the home is unsafe or they are treated disrespectfully, no refund is due for the time already worked and we may keep the full Booking price.

8.8 Our Cancellations, Payment and Refunds Policy sets out these rules in full, including how and when refunds are paid. It forms part of these terms.

9. Your responsibilities

9.1 You must give the Cleaner safe access to your home and the areas to be cleaned, and tell them about hazards such as broken fittings, wet floors, pets or unsafe areas.

9.2 Please put away valuables, cash, fragile items and anything of sentimental value. Please keep pets secure if the Cleaner asks.

9.3 You must treat our Cleaners with respect. We do not tolerate harassment, discrimination, threats or violence. We may refuse to provide the service to anyone who behaves in this way.

10. If something is not right (our guarantee)

10.1 If a Booking is not carried out with reasonable care and skill, or does not match what we agreed, tell us within 48 hours by email or through the platform. Photos help.

10.2 We will arrange a re-clean of the affected areas at no extra charge. If we cannot do this, or the re-clean does not put things right, we will refund you for the affected part of the Booking, or the whole Booking if appropriate.

10.3 This guarantee is in addition to your legal rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, including your right to have the service repeated, or to a price reduction. It does not affect them.

11. Damage and insurance

11.1 Please report any damage or loss within 48 hours of the Booking, with photos if you can. We will investigate fairly and quickly.

11.2 If we or a Cleaner are legally responsible for damage or loss, we will put it right, or pay reasonable compensation through our insurance or ours and the Cleaner's.

11.3 We are not responsible for damage that was there before the visit, for normal wear and tear, for fragile or valuable items you did not tell us about, or for items that were not secured, unless the law says otherwise.

12. Loyalty rewards

12.1 Free hours. After you complete 10 paid Bookings within 12 calendar months, you earn 2 hours of Standard Cleaning free. The free hours must be used within 6 months of being earned. If you want a longer clean, you pay for the extra hours at our usual price. This is a one-off reward for each customer account.

12.2 If you do not complete 10 Bookings within 12 calendar months, the count restarts from your next Booking.

12.3 5% off. From your 11th completed Booking onwards, you receive 5% off the price of every later Booking, for as long as you keep booking with us. The 5% applies to the Booking price only, not to tips or the Products Add-on.

12.4 Only completed and paid Bookings count. Cancelled, unpaid and refunded Bookings do not.

12.5 Loyalty rewards cannot be combined with other offers, apart from the referral discount in clause

13. They have no cash value and cannot be transferred.

12.6 We may change or end the loyalty rewards by giving you at least 30 days' notice. Rewards you have already earned will be honoured.

13. Referring friends

13.1 If you refer a new household to us through your personal link or code, you both get £10. The reward is paid in two parts: £5 after your friend's first Booking is completed and paid, and £5 after their second. Your friend receives £5 off their first booking and £5 off their second.

13.2 If you are a customer and have not registered as a Partner, your reward is given as Booking Credit, applied to your next Booking on the platform. It is not paid in cash.

13.3 Booking Credit has no cash value, cannot be transferred, and is lost if your account is closed. Booking Credit expires 12 months after it is issued.

13.4 A new household is one that has never been booked with us. A referral must be made through your link or code before your friend books. You cannot refer yourself or someone who lives at your address. We do not pay a reward on a Booking that is cancelled, unpaid or refunded.

13.5 If you would like to earn gift cards instead, you can register as a Partner and the Partner Programme terms will apply to you.

14. Complaints

14.1 If you are unhappy, please contact us at hello@opulencebliss.com. We will acknowledge your complaint within 3 working days and aim to reply in full within 14 days. Our Complaints Procedure explains each stage.

14.2 If we cannot resolve your complaint, we will tell you in writing. We do not currently use an alternative dispute resolution (ADR) provider. You can take legal action in the courts, and you can get free advice about your rights from Citizens Advice.

15. Your information (data protection)

15.1 We are the controller of your personal information. We are registered with the ICO under number ZC264981. Our privacy notice explains what we collect, why, who we share it with and how long we keep it.

15.2 We use your information to run your Bookings, take payment, keep you and our Cleaners safe, prevent fraud, meet our legal duties and, where you have agreed, send you offers.

15.3 We share your name, address, access details and relevant notes with your Cleaner so they can carry out the Booking. We share payment details only with Stripe.

15.4 You can ask to see, correct or delete your information, object to how we use it, withdraw your consent to marketing at any time, and complain to the ICO or any successor regulator. If you want to complain to us about how we handle your information, email hello@opulencebliss.com. We will acknowledge your complaint within 3 working days and reply without undue delay, and within 30 days in any case.

16. Our liability

16.1 Nothing in these terms excludes or limits our liability for death or personal injury caused by our negligence, for fraud, or for anything else that cannot be excluded by law. Nothing affects your legal rights as a consumer.

16.2 Subject to clause 16.1, we are responsible for foreseeable loss or damage caused by our breach of these terms or by our failure to use reasonable care and skill. We are not responsible for loss that was not foreseeable, or for any business losses, because we provide the service for domestic use only.

16.3 We are not responsible for delays or failures caused by events outside our reasonable control. We will tell you promptly if this affects a booking.

17. Changes to these terms

17.1 We may update these terms. We will give you at least 30 days' notice of changes that affect you. A change applies to Bookings made after it takes effect.

18. General

18.1 These terms are the whole agreement between us about our services and replace earlier discussions.

18.2 If any part is found to be unenforceable, the rest continues to apply.

18.3 If we delay in enforcing a right, we have not given it up.

18.4 You may not transfer your Booking to someone else without our written consent. We may transfer our rights to another company if it carries on the business, and we will tell you.

18.5 Only you and we have rights under these terms. Nobody else can enforce them under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999.

18.6 We may give you notices by email to the address on your account, and you may give us notices at hello@opulencebliss.com.

18.7 These terms are governed by the law of England and Wales. If you live in England or Wales, the courts of England and Wales have jurisdiction. If you live in Scotland or Northern Ireland, you may also bring legal action in the courts of your home country.

19. Contact us

3.4 We send you a confirmation and a receipt by email for every payment.

3.5 If a payment fails, we will tell you and may ask you to pay another way. A Booking may not go ahead until payment is made. 12.2 If we cannot resolve your complaint, we will tell you in writing. We do not currently use an alternative dispute resolution (ADR) provider. You can take legal action in the courts, and you can get free advice about your rights from Citizens Advice.

HANDYMAN SERVICES TERMS FOR CUSTOMERS Opulence Bliss Ltd | Version 1.0 | Effective from: 1 October 2026 These terms apply when you book handyman, repair or installation work through our platform. They are in addition to our Customer Terms and Conditions and our Cancellations, Payment and Refunds Policy. If there is a conflict on handyman work, these terms apply.

1. About these terms

1.1 These terms apply between Opulence Bliss Ltd ("we", "us", "our"), company number 15894675, registered office 128 City Road, London, United Kingdom, EC1V 2NX, and you, a household customer who books handyman work ("Job"). Contact: hello@opulencebliss.com.

1.2 Jobs are carried out by self-employed handymen ("Handyman") who meet our checks. We are responsible to you for the service under this contract.

1.3 Before we confirm a Job, we check each Handyman's identity, right to work, qualifications and registrations, basic DBS certificate and public liability insurance.

2. Quotes and booking

2.1 You describe the Job and send photos or videos if you can. A Handyman gives you a written Quote through the platform, showing the price for Labour (workmanship and time) and for Materials separately. The Quote shows the total you will pay. We do not charge a call-out fee or booking fee.

2.2 A Quote is open for 30 days unless it says otherwise. A contract for the Job starts when you accept the Quote and book a date, and we confirm it by email.

2.3 Some Jobs need the Handyman to see the work before quoting. We do not charge for a site visit to give a Quote. If you cancel an agreed site visit with less than 24 hours' notice, we may ask for a fair contribution towards the Handyman's time, which we will tell you about first.

2.4 If the Job turns out to need more time or materials than the Quote, the Handyman must tell you and get your agreement through the platform before doing any extra work. You will not be charged for anything you have not agreed to.

3. Materials

3.1 You can buy the Materials yourself, or pay us for them and the Handyman will buy them. If the Handyman buys them, you pay the cost shown on the receipt, at cost, with no mark-up from us.

3.2 The Materials estimate in the Quote may change only with your agreement (clause 2.4). If the final cost is lower, we refund or credit the difference.

3.3 Materials that have been bought and fitted, or specially ordered for you, are paid for in full. Materials that are unused and can be returned will be refunded.

3.4 Where you choose the Materials against the Handyman's advice, the Handyman is not responsible for faults caused by those Materials.

4. Payment

4.1 We take payment by card through Stripe when you accept the Quote and book. For larger Jobs, the Quote may split the Labour into stages. We will tell you before each payment is taken.

4.2 We are not registered for VAT, so no VAT is added.

4.3 Tips are optional and 100% goes to the Handyman.

4.4 Refunds are made as set out in our Cancellations, Payment and Refunds Policy, within 14 days.

5. Gas, electrical and other regulated work

5.1 Gas work is carried out only by a Handyman on the Gas Safe Register for that work. Notifiable electrical work is carried out only by a Handyman registered with a competent person scheme, or the work is notified to Building Control as the law requires. You can ask to see the Handyman's registration card or certificate.

5.2 After gas or electrical work, we make sure you get the proper certificate (for example a gas safety record, an Electrical Installation Certificate or a Minor Works Certificate) and any building-regulations notification. Please keep them safe, because you may need them to sell or let your home.

5.3 We do not carry out work involving asbestos or structural work. If the Handyman finds asbestos or an unsafe structure, they will stop and tell you.

5.4 If you are a landlord, you remain responsible for your own legal duties, such as gas safety checks. Our certificate does not replace advice from your lettings agent or solicitor.

6. Your responsibilities

6.1 You must give safe access to the property and the work area, tell us about hazards, pets, shut-off points (water, gas, electricity) and anything that could affect the Job, and make sure you have permission from the owner or landlord for the work.

6.2 Please protect valuables and clear the work area. Tell the Handyman if there is anything fragile or valuable nearby.

6.3 You must treat our Handymen with respect. We do not tolerate harassment, discrimination, threats or violence.

7. Your right to cancel within 14 days

7.1 Under the Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013, you have the right to cancel within 14 days of the date we confirm the Job, without giving a reason.

7.2 If you want the Job to start within the 14 days, you must ask us to start when you book. If you then cancel after work has started, you must pay for the work already done in proportion to the whole Job, and for Materials already bought.

7.3 If the Job is fully carried out within the 14 days at your express request, you can no longer cancel it.

7.4 Emergency repairs. If you ask us to attend urgently to deal with an emergency in your home, for example a burst pipe or a gas leak, and the work is done during the emergency, you cannot cancel that work, but you can cancel any other work you agree to on that visit.

7.5 To cancel, email hello@opulencebliss.com. We will refund what you have paid, less any amount due under this clause, within 14 days.

8. Changing or cancelling a Job

8.1 If you cancel after the 14-day period, what we refund of the Labour depends on your notice before the start:

• 48 hours or more: full refund

• 24 to 48 hours: 75% refund (25% charged)

• 12 to 24 hours: 50% refund (50% charged)

• Less than 12 hours, or on the day of the visit: no refund

8.2 We charge only the amount above, and no other fee. Materials are dealt with under clause 3.3.

8.3 We encourage you to reschedule a Job rather than cancel it. We also encourage our Handymen to do so.

8.4 If we or the Handyman cancel, we will refund you in full and offer you another time. If the Handyman does not attend and has not told us, we will refund you in full and treat your rebooking as a priority.

8.5 If something unavoidable happens, such as illness or an emergency, please tell us. We will consider each case fairly and will not charge you where it would be unreasonable.

9. Workmanship guarantee

9.1 The Handyman will carry out the Job with reasonable care and skill. We guarantee the workmanship for 30 days from completion.

9.2 If you find a defect in the workmanship in that time, tell us within 48 hours of noticing it if you can, with photos. We will arrange for it to be put right at no extra charge, usually within 7 days. If we cannot, we will refund you for the affected work.

9.3 The guarantee does not cover faults in Materials you chose against the Handyman's advice, damage caused by you or others after the Job, or normal wear and tear.

9.4 This guarantee is in addition to your legal rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, including to have the service repeated or to a price reduction. It does not affect them.

10. Damage and insurance

2.4 If the terms in our quote differ from these terms, the quote applies to the points it covers. Your own terms and conditions, or any purchase-order terms, do not apply unless we have agreed them in writing.

3.3 The Client must provide all cleaning supplies and equipment needed for the Services, including cleaning products, consumables (such as soap, shampoo, toilet roll and refills) and equipment (such as vacuum cleaners, mops, buckets and cloths), and must keep them available at the premises. 3.4 We invoice at the frequency stated in our quote (weekly, fortnightly or monthly), in advance or in arrears as agreed. 3.5 If you dispute an invoice, tell us within 7 days of receiving it and pay the part that is not in dispute. We will work with you to resolve the dispute quickly.

We may also charge interest and compensation under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998, which is interest at 8% above the Bank of England base rate and the fixed sum for recovery costs that the Act allows.

3.7 We may review prices once every 12 months, or sooner if there is a change in law (for example the National Minimum Wage or the National Living Wage) that affects our costs. If you want to end the Contract early for any other reason, you must pay an early termination fee of 25% of the fees that would have been due for the rest of the Minimum Term, up to a maximum of 3 months' fees. PRIVACY POLICY Opulence Bliss Ltd | Version 1.0 | Effective from: 1 October 2026 Peace within your walls.

1. Introduction

1.1 Opulence Bliss Ltd ("Opulence Bliss", "we", "our" or "us") respects your privacy and is committed to protecting your personal information.

1.2 This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, share, store and protect personal information when you:

• book or use our cleaning services (a Customer);

• apply to work with us or carry out bookings as a self-employed cleaner (a Cleaner) or handyman (a Handyman);

• apply for a job with us or work for us as a member of our team (a Job applicant or Team member);

• register as a Partner, or are referred to us by a Partner or another customer (a Partner or a Referred person);

• contract with us on behalf of a business (a Business customer);

• contact us, give feedback, make a complaint or otherwise deal with us.

1.3 For the purposes of UK data protection law, including the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR), the Data Protection Act 2018 and the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003 (PECR), as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, Opulence Bliss Ltd is the controller of the personal information described in this policy.

1.4 This policy should be read with our Customer Terms and Conditions, our Cleaner Terms and Conditions, our Handyman Terms and Conditions, our Partner Programme Terms and Conditions, our Cookie and Similar Technologies Policy, our DBS and Criminal-Offence Data Policy and our Safeguarding, Lone Working and Incident Policy.

1.5 In this policy, a reference to a Cleaner also applies to a Handyman unless we say otherwise. "Professionals" means Cleaners and Handymen.

2. Who we are and how to contact us

Opulence Bliss Ltd Company registration number: 15894675 (registered in England and Wales) Registered office: 128 City Road, London, United Kingdom, EC1V 2NX ICO registration number: ZC264981 Email: hello@opulencebliss.com Call, SMS or WhatsApp: +44 7484 717935 Website: www.opulencebliss.com If you have any questions about this policy or how we handle your personal information, please contact us using these details.

3. The systems we use

3.1 We run an online platform, website and mobile app that connect households and businesses with self-employed cleaners and handymen. We also manage our business using the following services:

• Google Workspace, including Gmail, Google Forms, Google Sheets, Google Calendar and Google Drive

• WhatsApp Business

• Stripe, for payments and payouts

• Supabase, for our back end: customer and cleaner accounts, bookings, chat, photos and reminders

• Resend, for sending booking confirmations, reminders and password reset emails

• Google, if you choose "Sign in with Google"

• Google (Gemini), which powers the chat assistant built into our website and app

• Accounting software

• Gift card and voucher providers, for Partner rewards

• A massage provider, Wellness by Anja, for an optional benefit for Professionals

• Identity, right-to-work and criminal record checking providers

3.2 These services help us manage bookings, communicate with customers, cleaners and Partners, keep business records and make payments.

4. Information we collect

The information we collect depends on how you deal with us. We aim to collect only what is reasonably necessary.

4.1 Customers

• Name, telephone number and email address

• Property address, postcode and type of property, number of bedrooms and bathrooms

• Cleaning requirements, preferred dates and times, and your instructions

• Access arrangements, such as key-safe codes and entry instructions

• Information about pets or anything that affects safety at your home

• For handyman jobs, a description of the job and any photos or videos you send us, the Quote, and the Materials you choose to buy or pay for

• Limited notes about your needs where they affect safety or how we serve you, for example "needs extra time at the door" (see section 4.7)

• Whether you want cleaning products (the Products Add-on)

• Booking history, cancellations, refunds, tips, loyalty rewards, referral rewards and Booking Credit

• Payment information (processed by Stripe)

• Reviews, feedback, complaints, damage reports and photos you send us, and messages you send through the app, including chat

• Our communications with you, including messages you send through the chat assistant

4.2 Cleaners and Handymen

• Name, date of birth, contact details and address

• Identity documents and right-to-work information

• The outcome of a basic Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check

• Self-employment and tax information, including your Unique Taxpayer Reference where you give it to us

• Proof of your public liability insurance

• For Handymen, your trade, qualifications and registrations, including your Gas Safe registration number and ID card details or your competent person scheme registration, where they apply

• Your emergency contact: their name, relationship to you and telephone number. You must tell them that you have given us their details

• When you check in, the time, and the distance between your phone's location and the booking address, so that we can confirm you are at the property (within 500 metres). We keep the time, the distance and the result of the check, not your exact coordinates. If you report a problem getting in, we record the same information. When you check out, we record only the time. We do not track your location at any other time. We also keep any message you send us about running late or being unable to check in

• References, experience, qualifications, availability and the areas you work in

• Bank account and payout information (processed by Stripe)

• Your bookings, hours, pay, tips, ratings and referral rewards

• Information about complaints, incidents or service quality

• Your choices about optional benefits, such as the massage benefit, and any amount taken from your referral rewards balance for it

4.3 Partners

• Name, email address and telephone number, and the details you give on the Partner sign-up form, including your consent

• The description you choose for yourself, for example cleaner, freelancer or stay-at-home parent

• Your personal referral link or code and your referral activity

• Your reward balance and the Gift Cards we send you

• Identity and email verification information

4.4 Referred people If a Partner or a customer gives us your details, or you contact us through a referral link or code, we receive your name and contact details and the fact that you were referred. We use this to contact you only if you asked us to, and to credit the referral. Partners must have your permission before they pass on your details.

4.5 Business customers The business name, the name, job title and contact details of the people we deal with, the property address, contract and invoice information, and payment details.

4.6 Information from other sources We may receive information from Stripe, identity and criminal record checking providers, insurers, referees, official online registers (such as the Gas Safe Register) and the Partner or customer who referred you.

4.7 Safeguarding, incident and safety records If a concern, accident, threat, theft allegation or other incident arises on a booking, we keep a record. It may include the names and contact details of the people involved, what happened, what was said, messages or photos relating to the incident, any notes about a person's needs that affected safety, and what we did next. It can include information about a child or a vulnerable adult, and sometimes health information, but only what we need to keep people safe. The records are described in our Safeguarding, Lone Working and Incident Policy.

4.8 Job applicants and our team If you apply for a job with us or work for us as a member of our team, we collect your name, contact details, application and CV, references, right-to-work and identity information, and, once you start, your employment and payment records. We give you a separate notice that explains this in full. Team members may see the information of Customers, Professionals and Partners, but only what they need to do their work.

5. How we use your information and our lawful bases

We must have a lawful basis under UK data protection law to use your personal information. Depending on the circumstances, we rely on the following.

5.1 Contract Where it is necessary to arrange or carry out a contract with you, or to take steps at your request before a contract. For example, to confirm and manage a booking, take payment, pay a Cleaner, send you a Gift Card, give you Booking Credit or provide customer support.

5.2 Legitimate interests Where it is reasonably necessary for our legitimate interests and these are not overridden by your rights. For example, to run and improve our services, match Customers with suitable Cleaners, keep records, investigate complaints and incidents, prevent fraud and misuse of referrals and rewards, protect Customers and Professionals (including through check-ins and emergency contacts), deal with safeguarding concerns and incidents, and recover amounts owed. You can object to this use. See section 17.

5.3 Legal obligation Where we must do something by law. For example, keeping accounting and tax records, carrying out right-to-work checks, and sharing information with HMRC or other authorities.

5.4 Consent Where the law requires it, we ask for your consent. For example, to send you marketing messages where PECR requires consent, or to share your details with the massage provider for the optional massage benefit. You can withdraw your consent at any time.

5.5 Criminal offence information The outcome of a basic DBS check is criminal offence information. We use it only to protect Customers and the public, and to prevent unlawful acts, and only where UK data protection law allows. Professionals apply for and pay for their own check and show us the certificate. Only the owner and our authorised onboarding team may see it. We keep a record of the outcome and the date, and we do not keep a copy of the certificate for longer than 6 months. See our DBS and Criminal-Offence Data Policy.

5.6 Special category information We do not ask for health information or other special category information. Please do not send us this unless it is necessary, for example if you tell us about an allergy that affects the cleaning products we use. If you or someone else gives it to us, we use it only to provide the service safely and, where relevant, to deal with a safeguarding concern or incident (see section 5.7).

5.7 Safeguarding and incident records We use these records under our legal duties and our legitimate interests in keeping people safe. Where they include special category information or criminal offence information, we rely on the conditions in Schedule 1 of the Data Protection Act 2018 for safeguarding children and individuals at

risk, and for preventing or detecting unlawful acts. We share them only where this is necessary to keep someone safe, or where the law requires or allows it.

6. Who we share your information with

6.1 Cleaners and Handymen. When a booking or job is accepted, we give the assigned Professional the information they need to do the job safely, such as your name, address, booking date and time, cleaning or job requirements, any job photos and access instructions.

6.2 Customers. We give Customers their Cleaner's or Handyman's first name, photograph and rating, so that they know who is coming. For handyman jobs, they also see the Quote.

6.3 Stripe. We use Stripe to take payments and pay Cleaners. Stripe may act as an independent controller for some purposes, such as verifying identity and preventing fraud, and its own privacy policy applies to that. We do not ask you for your online banking passwords or PINs, and you should never send them to us.

6.4 Gift Card providers. To send a Partner their Gift Card, we share their first name, email address and the Gift Card value with the gift card provider, who may be a reseller of cards from retailers such as Amazon, Tesco, Asda and Marks & Spencer. We delete Gift Card codes once they have been sent. The retailers are not connected with us, and their own gift card terms apply.

6.5 Identity, right-to-work and DBS check providers. To check Cleaners and Handymen. We check Gas Safe and other registrations on the official online registers.

6.6 Emergency contacts. If a Professional does not check in and we cannot reach them, we may contact their emergency contact, and, in a real emergency, the emergency services.

6.7 Insurers and brokers. If a claim or incident involves you.

6.8 The massage provider. If you are a Cleaner or Handyman and choose the optional massage benefit, we share your name, contact details, member reference and booking date with Wellness by Anja, an independent provider and a separate controller, with your consent. We pay the provider for each treatment from your referral rewards balance, with your agreement, and we keep a record of this. We do not collect or share health information about you. The provider is responsible for any information you give it directly, such as its intake form, and has its own privacy policy.

6.9 Our advisers and service providers. Accountants, solicitors, other professional advisers, and technical and IT service providers, including Google, WhatsApp, Supabase and Resend. They act on our instructions or under their own legal obligations.

6.10 Authorities. HMRC, the police, regulators and courts where the law requires, or where it is necessary to prevent or detect crime. UK rules on reporting by digital platforms may also require us to share information about Cleaners and their earnings with HMRC.

COMPLAINTS PROCEDURE For customers, business clients, cleaners, handymen and Partners | Opulence Bliss Ltd | Version 1.0 | Effective from: 1 October 2026 This is the single complaints procedure that applies to everything we do. It is referred to in our Customer Terms, Business Terms, Cleaner Terms, Handyman Terms, Partner Programme Terms and policies. We want to hear when something is wrong, so we can put it right.

1. Our promise

1.1 We take every complaint seriously, we treat it fairly, and we deal with it in the same way whoever you are. Making a complaint will never affect how we treat you. Cleaners, handymen and Partners will not be penalised, suspended or lose work for raising a complaint in good faith.

1.2 A complaint is any expression of dissatisfaction about our service, a booking, a cleaner or handyman, a payment, a refund, a reward, a price, our staff, or how we handle personal information.

2. Key response times

StageWhat happens and when
AcknowledgementWithin 3 working days of receiving your complaint
Full replyWithin 14 days of receiving it, where we can
Complex complaintsA full reply within 28 days, with an update to you by day 14
Data protection complaintsAcknowledged within 3 working days, and a reply within 30 days at the latest
Review of our replyRequested within 14 days of our reply, and the outcome sent within 14 days of your request
Urgent or safety mattersWe contact you the same day (see clause 5)

3. How to complain

3.1 Contact us in any of these ways:

• Email: hello@opulencebliss.com

• Phone or WhatsApp: +44 7484 717935

• Through your account or the platform

• By post: Opulence Bliss Ltd, 128 City Road, London, United Kingdom, EC1V 2NX

3.2 Please tell us your name, your booking or account reference, what went wrong, what you would like us to do, and any photos or messages that help. If you cannot give all this, tell us what you can and we will ask for the rest.

3.3 Please tell us as soon as you can, ideally within 30 days, so that we can find the facts. If a complaint is about the quality of a visit, tell us within the time in your terms (48 hours for household customers, 24 hours for business clients). We will still look at later complaints where we can.

3.4 You can ask someone to complain for you, such as a family member or an adviser. We will ask for your written permission. We will make reasonable adjustments if you find it hard to complain in writing, for example by taking your complaint by phone.

4. How we deal with it

Stage 1: Acknowledgement. Within 3 working days, we confirm we have your complaint, give it a reference number, and tell you who is dealing with it and when to expect a reply. Stage 2: Investigation and reply. We look at the facts, speak to everyone involved including the cleaner, handyman or Partner, and check our records. We send you a full written reply within 14 days. It explains what we found, what we will do, and why. If we need longer, we write to you by day 14 to say why and when to expect the reply, which will be within 28 days. Stage 3: Review. If you are not happy with our reply, tell us within 14 days. Someone who was not involved in the first reply will review it where we can. Where the owner dealt with the first reply, we will offer a review by an independent person, for example a mediator, if you would like one. We will send our final reply within 14 days of your request. Stage 4: Outside help. If we still cannot agree, you can:

• take legal action in the courts;

• use mediation, which we will take part in if you ask for it;

• get free advice from Citizens Advice (citizensadvice.org.uk or 0808 223 1133 in England); and

• for personal data, complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk, 0303 123 1113). We do not currently use an alternative dispute resolution (ADR) provider. If this changes, we will tell you.

5. Urgent matters

5.1 Contact us immediately by phone for:

• any danger, injury, assault, threat or harassment;

• a safeguarding concern about a child or an adult at risk;

• a theft allegation, lost or compromised keys or access codes; and

• a data breach.

5.2 We deal with these under our Safeguarding, Lone Working and Incident Reporting Policy and our data protection duties, and not only under this procedure. We will contact you the same day. If anyone is in immediate danger, call 999.

6. Complaints about people who work through us

6.1 If a complaint is about a cleaner or handyman, we will tell that person what has been said and give them the chance to respond, unless there is a safety reason not to. We may suspend them while we investigate. Suspension does not mean they are at fault.

6.2 If a complaint shows a possible crime or serious risk, we will tell the police or the right authority.

6.3 If a cleaner, handyman or Partner is the person complaining, for example about pay, rewards, cancellations or suspension, we will deal with it under this procedure and the same times apply. Cleaners and handymen can also ask for a review of a suspension decision within 14 days, as set out in their terms.

7. Complaints about personal information

7.1 If you are unhappy about how we use your personal information, tell us first. We will acknowledge your complaint within 3 working days, look into it, tell you the outcome without undue delay and within 30 days at the latest, and tell you if we need longer and why.

7.2 We will tell you what we found, what we will do, and about your right to complain to the ICO. This does not affect your right to complain to the ICO at any time.

8. What we can do to put things right

8.1 Depending on the complaint, we may: say sorry, explain what happened, redo the work, arrange another cleaner or handyman, refund all or part of a payment, give Booking Credit or a goodwill credit, correct a record or payment, pay a reward that was missed, change how we work, or take action against the person responsible.

8.2 We decide what is fair in each case. Any refund or credit follows our Cancellations, Payment and Refunds Policy and our terms, and this procedure does not reduce your legal rights.

9. Fairness, confidentiality and records

9.1 We keep complaints confidential and share them only with people who need to know, or where the law requires.

9.2 We record every complaint, the date, who dealt with it, what we decided and when we closed it. We keep these records for 6 years, or longer where the law requires.

9.3 We review the complaints log every 3 months, look for patterns and causes, and make changes to prevent the same problem happening again.

9.4 Our owner is responsible for this procedure. We review it at least once a year.

10. Letters we send

Acknowledgement. "Thank you for contacting Opulence Bliss. We have received your complaint (reference {number}) on {date}. {Name} is looking into it. We will reply in full by {date}. If you have more to tell us, please reply to this email." Reply. "Thank you for your complaint (reference {number}). We looked at {what we checked}. We found {findings}. We will {action}. If you are not happy with this reply, you can ask us to review it by writing to hello@opulencebliss.com within 14 days. After that you can also take legal action or use mediation, and you can get free advice from Citizens Advice. If your complaint is about personal information, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office at ico.org.uk."

11. Contact us

Opulence Bliss Ltd 128 City Road, London, United Kingdom, EC1V 2NX Company number: 15894675 ICO registration number: ZC264981 Telephone: +44 7484 717935 Email: hello@opulencebliss.com

1. About us and these terms

1.1 These terms apply between Opulence Bliss Ltd ("we", "us", "our") and each individual who registers as a Partner ("you").

1.2 Our details: Opulence Bliss Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales, company number

15894675. Registered office: 128 City Road, London, United Kingdom, EC1V 2NX.

Registered with the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) under number ZC264981. Contact: hello@opulencebliss.com.

1.3 We run an online platform that connects households and businesses in London with self-employed cleaners and handymen. As a Partner, you recommend our services to other people and may earn rewards when they buy.

1.4 In these terms:

• Household means an individual who books our services for their home.

• Business means a company, partnership, sole trader or other organisation that buys our services for business purposes, including offices, shops, landlords, lettings agents, serviced accommodation hosts and property managers.

• New customer means a Household or Business that has never booked or contracted with us before and whom we have not already been in contact with about our services.

• Referral means a new customer who contacts us or books through your personal link, code or referral form.

• Booking Credit means credit applied to a customer's next booking, as set out in clause 7.

1.5 By registering as a Partner, you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not register.

2. Becoming a Partner

2.1 Joining is free. There is no joining fee, no monthly fee and no charge for guidance, materials or support. You do not have to buy anything.

2.2 You must be at least 18 years old and living in the United Kingdom and able to receive Gift Cards at an email address that you control.

2.3 You apply by completing our registration form. Registering your interest does not guarantee that you will be accepted. We may accept or decline an application at our discretion, and we will tell you if we decline.

2.4 You must give us accurate information and keep it up to date. You may hold only one Partner account.

2.5 Before we give you a reward, we may need to verify your identity and email address. If you do not complete verification, we may delay your reward until you do.

2.6 Cleaners on our platform may also be Partners. Rewards for referring other cleaners are covered by the cleaner terms and not by these terms.

3. Your status: independent

3.1 You are an independent individual. Nothing in these terms makes you our employee, worker, partner in a legal partnership, agent or franchisee, and you have no authority to bind us, to agree prices or terms for us, or to make promises on our behalf.

3.2 You choose whether, when and how to promote us. We do not guarantee any number of customers or any level of reward, and there is no minimum amount of activity you must carry out.

3.3 We do not require you to work exclusively for us, and you remain free to promote other businesses, provided you follow clause 10.

4. Your referral link

4.1 We will give you a personal link or code. We use it to identify your referrals. You must not share it in a way that breaches clause 10.

4.2 A referral is counted only if it is made through your link, code or referral form before the person books or contracts with us. We cannot add referrals afterwards.

4.3 If more than one Partner or customer claims the same referral, we will credit the first valid referral recorded on our systems.

5. Referring households: the £10 reward

5.1 If you refer a new Household, you earn £10, and the Household receives £10 off their bookings. This is a one-off reward for each new Household.

5.2 The reward is paid in two parts. You earn £5 after the Household's first booking is completed and paid, and a further £5 after their second booking is completed and paid. The Household receives £5 off their first booking and £5 off their second booking. If the second booking is not completed and paid, the second part is not paid.

5.3 The reward does not apply to bookings made before the referral, to repeat bookings beyond the second, or to the same household more than once.

5.4 We do not pay a reward on a booking that is cancelled, unpaid or refunded, or if we reasonably believe the referral is not genuine, for example where you are the customer or a member of the same household.

6. Referring businesses: the percentage reward

6.1 If you refer a Business that becomes a new customer, you may earn a one-off reward based on the Business's first month's fee, as follows:

• 5% of the first month's fee for each of your first three qualifying Business referrals; and

• 10% of the first month's fee for your fourth qualifying Business referral and each one after that.

6.2 The higher rate applies only to your fourth and later qualifying referrals. It does not increase rewards for your first three.

6.3 A Business referral is qualifying only if:

• the Business is a new customer and you introduced it through your link, code or referral form before we had been in contact with it about our services;

• we accept the Business as a customer, which we may decline at our discretion;

• the Business signs a written service agreement with us that has a minimum term of 12 months;

• the Business's trial period (the first 4 weeks of the agreement) has ended without either party ending the agreement; and

• the Business has paid its first month's fee in cleared funds.

6.4 The first month's fee means the amount invoiced to the Business for the first month of services under its agreement, before VAT, and excluding tips, one-off add-ons, product charges, credits and discounts.

6.5 Qualifying Business referrals are counted in the order in which the first month's fee is paid, across the whole time you are a Partner.

6.6 The reward is a one-off payment for each Business referral. It is not paid again when the agreement renews or the Business pays later invoices.

6.7 A Business referral earns the reward in this clause 6. It does not also earn the household reward in clause 5.

6.8 We decide whether to accept a Business, the price and the terms of its agreement. You must not negotiate or promise prices, services or terms on our behalf.

6.9 If the Business's first month's fee is refunded, reversed or charged back, we may withhold the reward. If we have already paid it, we may deduct the amount from your future rewards. We will not ask you to repay it in cash, unless it was paid because of a breach of these terms or fraud.

7. Customers who refer: Booking Credit

7.1 If you are a customer who has not registered as a Partner and you refer a new customer, your reward is given as Booking Credit and not as cash.

7.2 Booking Credit is applied automatically to your next booking. It has no cash value, cannot be transferred or exchanged, and is lost if your customer account is closed. Booking Credit expires 12 months after it is issued.

7.3 If you are registered as a Partner, your rewards are given as Gift Cards under clause 8, even if you are also a customer.

7.4 Clauses 5 and 6 apply to customer referrals in the same way, including the two-part payment for referring a household.

8. How rewards are given (Gift Cards)

8.1 Rewards are paid monthly in arrears. We convert each reward into a digital gift card or voucher (a "Gift Card") of your choice from Amazon, Tesco, Asda or Marks & Spencer (or other retailers we add, subject to availability), and send it to the email address on your account. We will convert the rewards that became payable in the previous month.

8.2 Partner rewards are given only as Gift Cards. We do not offer a cash alternative, and a Gift Card cannot be exchanged for cash. If your rewards in a month are below the smallest value for which a Gift Card can be issued, we will add them to your reward for the next month.

8.3 We pay the cost of issuing your Gift Card. The full value of your reward is given to you.

8.4 We show each reward in your account with a clear breakdown of the referral, the date and the amount.

8.5 You must make sure the email address on your account is correct. We are not responsible for Gift Cards sent to an incorrect address that you supplied. The retailer's own gift card terms apply

to your Gift Card, including any expiry date and how it can be used. These retailers are not connected with us, do not sponsor or endorse the Partner Programme, and are not responsible for it. The Gift Card provider's own terms also apply, including any expiry date, and we are not responsible for the provider's service or for a Gift Card that is lost or stolen after we have sent it.

8.6 If we give you too much by mistake, we may deduct the value from your future rewards or ask you to repay it.

9. Tax and reporting

9.1 You are responsible for your own tax. We do not deduct tax or National Insurance from your rewards. A reward given as a Gift Card is still a reward, and you are responsible for declaring it where required.

9.2 You should keep records of what you earn and declare it to HMRC where required. Please check gov.uk or take advice about your own position, including any allowances that may apply.

9.3 Where UK law requires us to share information about you or your rewards with HMRC, you agree to give us the information we need.

10. How you must promote us

10.1 You must be honest, clear and fair. You must not make false or misleading claims about us, our cleaners, our prices or what other Partners earn.

10.2 You must not promise or imply income, guarantee earnings or use the word "guaranteed" about rewards.

10.3 You must make it clear that you may be rewarded for a recommendation. If you promote us online or on social media, you must label the post clearly, for example with "ad" or "paid partnership", in line with Advertising Standards Authority (ASA), Committee of Advertising Practice (CAP) and Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) guidance.

10.4 You must follow the unfair commercial practices rules in Part 4 of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. You must not post or ask for fake or misleading reviews, or hide that a review was rewarded.

10.5 You must not send unsolicited marketing messages, spam or bulk messages on our behalf. You must follow the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003 (PECR), including having the right permission before you send marketing by email, text or social media message, and respecting opt-outs and telephone preference registrations.

10.6 You may use only our approved materials, name and logo, and only to promote our services. You must not impersonate us, pretend to be our employee or agent, or create websites, social media accounts or adverts that could be mistaken for ours.

10.7 You must not bid on our name or brand terms in paid search, or use our name in a web address, without our written permission.

10.8 You must not promote us in a way that is unlawful, discriminatory, harmful or likely to bring us into disrepute, and you must not direct promotion at children.

10.9 If we ask you to remove or correct a post or advert that breaks these terms, you must do so promptly.

11. Rewards come from sales, not from recruitment

11.1 Rewards are paid only for customers and businesses that actually buy our services. We do not pay rewards for recruiting other Partners, and you do not earn from other Partners' referrals.

11.2 You do not have to pay anything, buy any stock or meet any target to become or remain a Partner.

12. Your information and the information you share (data protection)

12.1 We are the controller of the personal information you give us as a Partner. We are registered with the ICO under number ZC264981.

12.2 We use your information to assess your application, verify your identity, run the programme, pay you, prevent fraud, meet our legal duties and, where you have agreed, send you marketing. Our privacy notice explains this in more detail, including how long we keep information.

12.3 We share your information only where needed, with Gift Card and identity providers, professional advisers, regulators and law enforcement where required by law.

12.4 You must not give us another person's contact details unless that person has agreed that you can pass them on and has been told that we will contact them. You must not share the personal information of people who have not agreed.

12.5 You have rights over your information under UK data protection law, including to access, correct and delete it, to object to its use and to complain to the ICO or any successor regulator. If you want to complain to us about how we handle your information, please email hello@opulencebliss.com. We will acknowledge your complaint within 3 working days and reply without undue delay, and within 30 days in any case.

12.6 We send marketing messages only if you have agreed, and you can withdraw consent at any time.

13. Fraud and misuse

13.1 You must not refer yourself or anyone who lives at your address or shares your email address, make or encourage fake bookings or accounts, offer cash or other payments to make people book, or misuse your link, code or any promotion.

13.2 If we reasonably believe you have broken this clause, we may withhold rewards, deduct rewards already paid from future rewards, suspend or close your account and, where appropriate, report the matter to the authorities.

14. Changes to rewards and these terms

14.1 We may change these terms, the rewards, or the programme by giving you at least 30 days' written notice.

14.2 A change does not reduce a reward on a referral that was already made before the date of the notice, as long as the customer books or the Business signs within 90 days of that date.

14.3 If you keep promoting us after a change takes effect, you accept it. If you do not agree, you can close your account.

15. Suspension and ending your account

15.1 You can close your account at any time by emailing hello@opulencebliss.com. We can end this agreement by giving you 14 days' written notice.

15.2 We may suspend or close your account immediately if you seriously break these terms, act dishonestly, or put us or others at risk.

15.3 When your account ends, we will give you the rewards that you had already earned under clauses 5 and 6, subject to clauses 6.9, 8.6 and 13.2. Referrals made through your link after your account closes do not earn rewards.

15.4 Clauses 6.9, 8.6, 9, 12, 13, 16, 17 and 19 continue to apply after your account ends.

16. Liability

16.1 Nothing in these terms excludes or limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud or for anything else that cannot be excluded by law.

16.2 Subject to clause 16.1, we are not liable for loss of earnings, loss of rewards that you expected but did not earn, or any indirect loss. Our total liability to you in connection with these terms is limited to the rewards we owe you.

16.3 We do not promise that any person you refer will book, or that we will accept any Business. We are not responsible for your costs of promoting us.

17. Intellectual property

17.1 Our name, logo, website and materials belong to us. We give you a limited, revocable permission to use our approved materials only to promote our services as set out in these terms. This permission ends when your account ends.

18. Complaints and disputes

18.1 If you have a complaint, including about a reward, please email hello@opulencebliss.com within 30 days. We will acknowledge it within 3 working days and aim to reply in full within 14 days. Our Complaints Procedure explains each stage.

18.2 If we cannot resolve a dispute, we will try mediation before either of us goes to court.

19. General

19.1 These terms are the whole agreement between us on this subject and replace earlier discussions.

19.2 If any part is found to be unenforceable, the rest continues to apply.

19.3 If we delay in enforcing a right, we have not given it up.

19.4 You may not transfer your rights or duties under these terms without our written consent. We may transfer ours to another company if it carries on the business.

19.5 Only you and we have rights under these terms. Nobody else can enforce them under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999.

19.6 We are not responsible for delay or failure caused by events outside our reasonable control.

19.7 We may give you notices by email to the address on your account, and you may give us notices at hello@opulencebliss.com.

19.8 These terms and any dispute arising from them are governed by the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction.

CLEANER CANCELLATION POLICY Opulence Bliss Ltd | Version 1.0 | Effective from: 1 October 2026 This policy forms part of the Cleaner Terms and Conditions. It applies to self-employed cleaners who accept Bookings through our platform.

1. Why this policy exists

1.1 When a Cleaner accepts a Booking, the customer and Opulence Bliss Ltd ("we", "us", "our") rely on that Booking going ahead. A cancelled visit leaves a household without a clean at short notice and can cost us a refund, so we set out the rules clearly here.

1.2 You are self-employed. You choose which Bookings to accept. This policy applies once you have accepted a Booking. Nothing in it requires you to accept any Booking or to work any minimum number of hours.

1.3 Terms such as "Booking" and "Cleaner" have the same meaning as in the Cleaner Terms and Conditions and the Customer Terms and Conditions.

2. Cancelling a Booking you have accepted

2.1 If you cannot attend a Booking, tell us as soon as you can through the platform or by emailing hello@opulencebliss.com. The more notice you give, the easier it is for us to find another Cleaner for the customer.

2.2 We encourage you to reschedule a Booking with the customer, rather than cancel it, wherever you can. A Booking moved to a new time that the customer agrees to is not a cancellation.

2.3 You have 2 grace cancellations in each calendar month. A grace cancellation is a cancellation of an accepted Booking that has no consequence for your account. The grace cancellations do not carry over to the next month.

2.4 We do not charge Cleaners for cancelling. If you cancel a third accepted Booking in the same calendar month, we may suspend your account under clause 5 instead.

2.5 Cancellations made by us, or because the customer cancelled, do not count towards your two grace cancellations, and your account is not affected.

3. Cancellations that do not count

3.1 The cancellation does not count towards the monthly limit, where you cannot attend because of:

• your own sudden illness or injury, an emergency involving you or a close family member, or a bereavement;

• an unsafe home, unsafe conditions at the property or unacceptable behaviour by the customer, reported to us promptly;

• transport disruption or severe weather that makes safe travel impossible; or

• a reason beyond your reasonable control.

3.2 Please tell us as soon as you can, and give us a short explanation. We may ask for reasonable evidence for repeated cases but will not ask for medical details beyond what is needed.

4. No-shows

4.1 A no-show means you do not attend an accepted Booking and do not tell us before it starts.

4.2 A no-show may lead to suspension under clause 5, whether or not you have used your grace cancellations. We will contact you to understand what happened before we decide.

4.3 If you cannot arrive on time, tell us and the customer as early as you can. Arriving late is not a cancellation, but repeated lateness may be dealt with under clause 5.

5. Repeated cancellations and suspension

5.1 We may suspend or close your account if there is a pattern of cancellations or no-shows, or a single serious incident, for example:

• one no-show where you did not tell us before the visit;

• three cancellations in the same calendar month; or

• cancelling Bookings in order to take the work directly from the customer outside the platform.

5.2 Before suspending your account, we will tell you why, give you the chance to explain, and take your explanation into account, unless there is a serious safety risk.

5.3 We will give you a written decision and reasons. If you disagree, you can ask us to review it by emailing hello@opulencebliss.com within 14 days. We will reply within 14 days.

5.4 Suspension or closure does not remove your right to be paid for work you have already done properly.

6. When the customer cancels

6.1 If a customer cancels late and we charge them under the Cancellations, Payment and Refunds Policy, you are paid your usual rate for the Booking in the same proportion. For example, if the customer is charged 50% of the Booking, you receive 50% of what you would have earned for it.

6.2 You may decide to charge the customer less than the full amount, or nothing, for example to keep a good relationship. If you do, tell us before the Booking time or within 24 hours afterwards. We will then reduce your pay in line with your decision and refund the customer the difference.

6.3 We encourage customers and Cleaners to reschedule a Booking rather than cancel it. If you agree a new time with the customer, no cancellation charge applies.

6.4 If the customer cannot be reached or does not let you in, wait 15 minutes, try to contact them through the platform and tell us. We will confirm whether the Booking counts as completed.

7. Fairness, status and changes

7.1 Nothing in this policy makes you our employee or worker. You decide whether to accept or decline work. If you cannot attend, tell us as set out in clause 2.1. To protect customers, only Cleaners who have passed our identity, right-to-work and DBS checks may enter a customer's home. You therefore cannot send a substitute. If you cannot attend, we will offer the Booking to another Cleaner who has already passed our checks.

7.2 We may change this policy by giving you at least 30 days' written notice. A change applies to Bookings you accept after it takes effect.

8. Contact us
