HANDYMAN TERMS AND CONDITIONS Opulence Bliss Ltd | Version 1.0 | Effective from: 1 October 2026 These terms are for self-employed handymen and trades who carry out repair, maintenance and installation work through our platform. They include our Cancellation and Suspension rules (clause 9).

1. About us and these terms

1.1 These terms apply between Opulence Bliss Ltd ("we", "us", "our") and each person who joins our platform as a handyman ("you"). We are a company registered in England and Wales, company number 15894675, registered office 128 City Road, London, United Kingdom, EC1V 2NX. ICO registration number: ZC264981. Contact: hello@opulencebliss.com.

1.2 We run an online platform that connects households and businesses in London with self-employed cleaners and handymen. Cleaners are covered by our Cleaner Terms and Conditions.

1.3 In these terms:

• Job means a piece of handyman work that a customer books through the platform.

• Quote means the price you give a customer for a Job through the platform. It has two parts: Labour (your workmanship and time) and Materials.

• Regulated Work means work that the law says only a registered or qualified person may do, including gas work and notifiable electrical work.

1.4 You accept these terms by ticking the box and selecting "I accept" when you register, or by accepting your first Job. We keep a record of the date and the version you accepted. If you do not agree, please do not join.

2. Eligibility and checks

2.1 You must be at least 18 years old and have the legal right to work or to carry out self-employed work in the United Kingdom.

2.2 Before you take Jobs, we will check your identity and right to work, review your experience, and ask for proof of your qualifications and registrations (see clause 3).

2.3 You must have a current basic Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check, which you apply for yourself and pay for, at https://www.gov.uk/request-copy-criminal-record. You must show us your certificate before your first Job. We handle this information as set out in clause 14 and in our DBS and criminal-offence data policy.

2.4 You must tell us promptly if anything you have told us changes, including any caution, conviction, restriction on your registration or loss of insurance.

2.5 We may refuse an application or repeat any check at any time.

3. Qualifications, registration and Regulated Work

3.1 You may only accept Jobs that you are properly qualified, trained, insured and, where the law requires, registered to carry out. You must not take on or quote for work outside your competence.

3.2 Gas work. You may carry out gas work only if you are on the Gas Safe Register for the type of work involved. You must show us your Gas Safe ID card and registration number, and keep

your registration current. You must give the customer a gas safety record or certificate where the law requires.

3.3 Electrical work. You may carry out notifiable electrical work (work covered by Part P of the Building Regulations) only if you are registered with a competent person scheme, or the work is notified to Building Control as the law requires. You must show us proof of your registration or qualification, and give the customer the right certificate (for example an Electrical Installation Certificate or Minor Works Certificate) and any building-regulations notification.

3.4 Other regulated work. This includes, for example, certain water-fittings work, work on fire safety equipment, and work that needs building control or other approval. Where a registration or notification is needed, you must have it and keep it current.

3.5 Without the right registration you must not carry out gas work or notifiable electrical work, however small it seems. If you do, we may close your account immediately.

3.6 We do not allow Jobs involving asbestos, structural work or work at height beyond what you are trained and equipped for, and you must stop and tell us if you find asbestos or an unsafe structure.

3.7 You must keep your documents current and send us renewed copies. We may suspend your account if a registration or certificate lapses.

4. Your status: self-employed

4.1 You are self-employed. Nothing in these terms makes you our employee, worker, partner or agent, and you have no authority to bind us.

4.2 You choose which jobs to accept and when. We do not guarantee any minimum amount of work. You may work for other clients and other platforms, subject to clause 12.

4.3 You use your own tools, equipment and vehicle, and you decide how to carry out each Job, within the standards in these terms and the law.

4.4 You are responsible for your own tax and National Insurance, for registering with HMRC as self-employed where required, and for your own insurance and tools. We do not deduct tax from what we pay you.

5. Quotes and Jobs

5.1 Jobs are offered through the platform. You assess the Job (from the customer's photos, video, description or a visit) and give a written Quote through the platform, showing Labour and Materials separately.

5.2 The Quote must be fair and clear, and you must not exceed it without the customer's agreement. If the Job changes or turns out to need more time or materials, you must tell us and the customer and get the customer's agreement through the platform before you do the extra work.

5.3 A Job is confirmed when the customer accepts your Quote and books a date. Quotes are open for 30 days unless they say otherwise.

5.4 You must arrive on time, work safely and to a good standard, keep the area tidy and respect the customer's home and belongings. You must photograph the work before and after, where reasonable, and keep records.

5.5 You must keep to the agreed scope. You must not do work the customer has not agreed or leave the Job unfinished without good reason.

6. Pay and commission

6.1 Labour. We take 25% commission on the Labour part of each Quote. You receive 75% of the Labour. The commission is taken from the Labour only. For example, if the labour is £200, you receive £150.

6.2 Materials. We take no commission and no mark-up on Materials. You receive back what you paid for the Materials, at cost, as set out in clause 7.

6.3 We pay the payment-processing costs on payments to you. They are not deducted from your pay.

6.4 You can choose to be paid weekly, every two weeks or monthly, by bank transfer through Stripe. There is no minimum payout. Each payment shows a breakdown of Labour, commission, Materials reimbursed, tips and any agreed deductions.

6.5 You are paid for Jobs that are completed and paid for by the customer. We may withhold or reduce payment for a Job that was not completed, was cancelled by you without proper notice, or where the customer is refunded because of your breach or poor workmanship.

6.6 We may change the commission or other terms by giving you at least 30 days' written notice. A change does not affect Quotes already accepted.

7. Materials

7.1 For each Job, the Quote states the Materials and their estimated cost. The customer may buy the materials themselves, or pay us for them, in which case you buy them.

7.2 If you buy the Materials, you must keep the receipt and upload it to the platform. We pay you the amount on the receipt, up to the Materials amount in the accepted Quote, with your next payout. We may agree in writing to pay you in advance for larger orders.

7.3 You must buy suitable materials of reasonable quality at a fair price. You must not buy more than the Job needs.

7.4 If the Materials cost more than the Quote, you must get the customer's agreement before you buy them. We pay you the extra only if the customer agrees.

7.5 If Materials are unused, or the Job is cancelled before they are fitted, you must return them where possible and we will refund the customer. If they cannot be returned, we deal with the cost under the customer terms and your clause 9 rights.

7.6 Materials you bought remain yours until the customer has paid for them.

8. Tips

8.1 Tips are voluntary. You keep 100% of tips. We take no share and deduct no fees. Tips are paid in your next payout and are your own income to declare to HMRC where required.

9. Cancellations, no-shows and suspension

9.1 We encourage you to reschedule a Job with the customer rather than cancel it. A Job moved to a new time that the customer agrees is not a cancellation.

9.2 You have 2 grace cancellations in each calendar month. We do not charge you for cancelling, but if you cancel a third accepted Job in the same calendar month, we may suspend your account.

9.3 A no-show, meaning you do not attend and do not tell us before the visit, may lead to suspension.

9.4 These cancellations do not count towards the limit: your own sudden illness or injury, an emergency involving you or a close family member, a bereavement, an unsafe home or unacceptable behaviour by the customer (reported promptly), transport disruption or severe weather, or a reason beyond your control. Tell us as soon as you can.

9.5 Before we suspend your account, we will tell you why and give you the chance to explain, unless there is a serious safety risk. We will give you written reasons, and you can ask for a review within 14 days.

9.6 When a customer cancels late. If the customer cancels and is charged under our customer cancellation rules, you are paid your usual share of the Labour in the same proportion. You may choose to charge the customer less, or nothing. Tell us before the visit or within 24 hours afterwards, and we will adjust your pay and refund the customer.

9.7 If the customer cancels after you have ordered special or non-returnable Materials, we reimburse you for them at cost, with receipts.

10. Standards of conduct and safety

10.1 You must act honestly, safely, lawfully and respectfully. Harassment, discrimination, violence, theft, working under the influence of drink or drugs and any breach of customer privacy are not tolerated.

10.2 You must work safely and follow health and safety law, assess risks before each Job, use suitable personal protective equipment, and report accidents, damage and safeguarding concerns to us promptly. You must follow our Safeguarding, Lone Working and Incident Reporting Policy.

10.3 You must keep customers' keys, access codes and personal information secure and use them only for the Job.

10.4 You must not take away waste unless you hold a waste carrier registration. Otherwise, you must leave the waste with the customer or arrange legal disposal with them.

11. Workmanship guarantee

11.1 You must carry out each Job with reasonable care and skill. You guarantee your workmanship for 30 days from completion.

11.2 If the customer reports a defect in your workmanship within that time, you must put it right at no extra charge within a reasonable time, usually within 7 days of being told.

11.3 If you do not put it right, we may arrange another handyman to do so, and deduct their reasonable cost from your pay, up to the Labour you were paid for that Job. We will tell you in writing before we do this.

11.4 The guarantee does not cover faults in Materials the customer insisted on against your advice, or damage caused by the customer or another person after the Job.

11.5 This does not limit the customer's legal rights, or yours.

12. Keeping customers on the platform

12.1 Customers introduced to you through the platform are customers of the platform. While you work with us and for 12 months after your account closes, you must not take, or offer to take, work from those customers outside the platform, ask or encourage them to stop using it, or accept payment from them other than through the platform for work arising from a platform Job.

12.2 This does not apply to customers you served before joining us and told us about in writing when you applied, or to work a customer asks you to do after leaving the platform for reasons unconnected to you.

12.3 If you break this clause, we may close your account, withhold unpaid amounts that arise from the breach, and take any other action the law allows.

13. Insurance and liability

13.1 We hold public liability insurance for our business. You must hold your own public liability insurance, with cover of at least £2,000,000 for any one claim, that covers the type of work you do (including any gas or electrical work), before your first Job and for as long as you work through the platform. You must send us a copy of your certificate when you apply and at each renewal, and tell us at once if it is cancelled or changed. If your cover lapses, we may suspend your account until you give us proof.

13.2 Our insurance does not replace yours, and we do not promise that it covers any claim arising from your work. You must not do anything that invalidates your cover.

13.3 You are responsible for loss or damage you cause by your own negligence or breach of these terms, and you must report any incident promptly.

13.4 Nothing in these terms excludes or limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud or for anything else that cannot be excluded by law.

13.5 Subject to clause 13.4, we are not liable for loss of earnings, loss of Jobs or any indirect loss, and our total liability to you in connection with these terms is limited to the amounts we owe you.

14. Your information (data protection)

14.1 We are the controller of the personal information you give us. We are registered with the ICO under number ZC264981.

14.2 We use your information to assess your application, check qualifications and registrations, run Jobs, pay you, prevent fraud, keep customers and handymen safe, meet our legal duties and, with your consent, send you marketing.

14.3 We share it only where needed, with payment providers such as Stripe, checking and insurance providers, professional advisers and regulators. We share limited information with customers, such as your first name, photograph, registrations and rating.

14.4 We keep your DBS outcome and certificate date as set out in our DBS and criminal-offence data policy, and do not keep a copy of the certificate for longer than the period in that policy.

14.5 You have rights over your information under UK data protection law. Our privacy notice, available on our website, explains how to use them. If you want to complain to us about how we handle your information, email hello@opulencebliss.com. We will acknowledge your complaint within 3 working days and reply without undue delay, and within 30 days in any case. You may also complain to the ICO.

15. Tax and reporting

15.1 You are responsible for your own tax. UK rules on reporting by digital platforms may require us to share information about you and your earnings with HMRC. You agree to give us the information needed to do so.

16. Ending your account

16.1 You can close your account at any time by giving us 7 days' written notice. We can end this agreement by giving you 14 days' written notice.

16.2 We may suspend or close your account immediately if you seriously breach these terms, work without a required registration, act dishonestly or unsafely, put a customer at risk, make false claims or commit fraud.

16.3 When your account ends, we will pay you for Jobs completed and reimburse your Materials, subject to clauses 6.5, 11.3 and 12.3. Clauses 12, 13, 14 and 15 continue to apply.

17. Changes, complaints and general

17.1 We may update these terms by giving you at least 30 days' notice of changes that affect your pay. If you keep working with us after a change takes effect, you accept it. If you do not agree, you can close your account.

17.2 If you have a complaint, including about a payment, contact hello@opulencebliss.com within 30 days. We will acknowledge it within 3 working days and aim to reply in full within 14 days. Our Complaints Procedure explains each stage. If we cannot resolve a dispute, we will try mediation before either of us goes to court.

17.3 These terms are the whole agreement between us on this subject. If any part is unenforceable, the rest continues to apply. You may not transfer your rights without our consent. Only you and we have rights under these terms under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999. They are governed by the law of England and Wales, and its courts have exclusive jurisdiction.

SAFEGUARDING, LONE WORKING AND INCIDENT REPORTING POLICY For cleaners and handymen | Opulence Bliss Ltd | Version 1.0 | Effective from: 1 October 2026 This policy sets out how we keep customers, and the cleaners and handymen who work in their homes, safe. It forms part of the Cleaner Terms and Conditions and the Handyman Terms and Conditions. In this policy "you" means a cleaner or handyman working through our platform.

1. Why this policy matters

1.1 You work alone, inside people's homes and businesses. That brings two kinds of risk: risk to your own safety, and risk to customers who may be vulnerable, such as older people, disabled people, people who are unwell and children.

1.2 We take both seriously. This policy tells you what to expect from us, what we expect from you, and exactly what to do when something goes wrong.

1.3 If anyone is in immediate danger, call 999 first. Then tell us.

2. Who is responsible

2.1 Our Safeguarding Lead is the owner of Opulence Bliss Ltd. They receive all safeguarding concerns and incident reports, decide what happens next, and keep the records. Contact: hello@opulencebliss.com or +44 7484 717935.

2.2 Our onboarding team explains this policy to every new cleaner and handyman and keeps records of who has been briefed.

2.3 Everyone who works through the platform is responsible for following this policy and for reporting concerns. You are not expected to investigate or to decide whether something is abuse. Your job is to notice, to keep people safe, and to tell us.

3. Who we mean by vulnerable

3.1 A child is anyone under 18.

3.2 An adult at risk is an adult who needs care and support, and who is experiencing, or is at risk of, abuse or neglect, and is unable to protect themselves because of those needs. This can include people with dementia, a physical or learning disability, a mental health condition, or frailty, and people who are isolated.

3.3 Vulnerability can be temporary, for example after an illness or bereavement. Treat everyone with respect, and take extra care where you notice signs that someone may need extra help.

3.4 We do not ask customers about health conditions when they book. If a customer tells us, or you notice, we may note only what is needed to keep them safe, such as "needs extra time at the door" or "hard of hearing".

4. Before a booking

4.1 Every cleaner and handyman has been through our checks: identity, right to work, a basic DBS certificate and insurance. A basic DBS check does not cover everything, so it does not replace your own vigilance.

4.2 If a customer tells us before a booking that they are vulnerable or live with someone who is, we will, where we can send the same cleaner or handyman each time, and tell you any practical needs.

4.3 You must give us an emergency contact when you register, and keep it up to date.

4.4 You will receive the address, date, time and any access or safety notes through the platform. Do not accept a booking if you do not feel safe doing so.

5. Working with vulnerable customers

5.1 Always treat the customer with dignity and respect. Speak clearly and calmly, use their name, and give them time to answer.

5.2 You are there to clean or to do repair work. Do not provide personal care, such as washing, dressing, toileting, feeding or giving medicines, and do not give medical advice. If a customer asks for this, politely decline and tell us.

5.3 Do not take, handle or hold money, bank cards, PINs, cheque books or valuables. Do not accept gifts of value, loans or any request to be added to a will or given power of attorney. Do not offer or ask for personal favour. Tell us if anyone asks you to do any of these things.

5.4 Do not take photographs of the customer, of other people in the home or of their personal belongings. Photograph the work only, where the terms allow, and keep other people out of the picture.

5.5 Where children are present, you must never be alone with a child, never provide childcare, and never be in a child's bedroom or bathroom while they are in it. Keep to the areas you have been asked to work in.

5.6 Do not share a customer's personal details, health or circumstances with anyone except us, or the emergency services if needed.

5.7 Respect a customer's choices. Do not move or touch medication, medical equipment, mobility aids or documents unless the customer asks and it is safe.

5.8 If a customer seems confused, distressed or unwell, stay calm. If they need urgent medical help, call 999. Then tell us.

6. What to look for and what to do

6.1 Signs that a customer may be at risk include:

• unexplained injuries, bruises or marks, or poor hygiene and neglect;

• being very afraid of, or controlled by, another person;

• missing money or belongings, or sudden changes to their finances;

• no food, heating or care, or unsafe living conditions;

• being locked in, or not allowed to speak for themselves;

• a child who seems fearful, hungry, unsupervised or injured, or who tells you something worrying.

6.2 If you see something that worries you:

• Immediate danger: call 999.

• Otherwise, tell the Safeguarding Lead the same day, and as soon as you safely can. Use the platform or call +44 7484 717935.

• Write down what you saw or heard, with the date, time and place. Record facts and the person's own words, not your opinions.

• Do not confront anyone, investigate, promise to keep a secret, or tell other people. If someone tells you something serious, listen, stay calm, say you are glad they told you, and explain that you must pass it on to keep them safe.

6.3 We will decide what to do, which may include contacting the local authority adult safeguarding team or children's services, the police, or the customer's family or doctor, depending on the situation. We will tell you what we need from you. You will not be punished for raising a concern in good faith, even if it turns out to be mistaken.

6.4 Helpful national numbers: NSPCC helpline 0808 800 5000 (children); Action on Elder Abuse 080 8808 8141. The local authority safeguarding team for the customer's borough can also be contacted.

7. Concerns about a cleaner or handyman

7.1 If a customer or anyone else raises a concern about a cleaner or handyman, we take it seriously and act promptly.

7.2 We may suspend the person from bookings while we look into it, which is not a finding that they did anything wrong. We will tell them what is being said, give them the chance to respond, and decide fairly.

7.3 Where the concern involves a possible crime or serious risk, we will tell the police or the right authority. Where needed, we will also tell the person's customers.

7.4 If you have a concern about how we or another cleaner or handyman is working, tell us. If you feel you cannot, you can contact the relevant local authority or the police.

8. Lone working: staying safe

8.1 Before you go. Check the booking details and any notes. Make sure your phone is charged and has the platform open. Tell us if you are running late.

8.2 Check in and out. Check in on the platform when you arrive and check out when you leave. If your plans change, tell us.

8.3 At the door. Trust your instincts. Do not go in if the customer seems drunk, aggressive or unsafe, if someone else at the property makes you uneasy, or if the situation is not as the booking said. You can leave at any time, and you will not be penalised. Tell us straight away.

8.4 While you work. Know where the exits are and keep your route to the door clear. Keep your phone, keys and valuables with you. Do not let anyone stand between you and the exit. Do not work in a locked room, and do not go into areas you are not asked to work in. Handymen must follow safe-working rules for ladders, tools, electricity, gas and water, and must not work at height beyond their training.

8.5 Pets and hazards. Ask the customer to secure pets. Report broken fittings, wet floors, mould, pests, needles and other hazards, and stop if you are not safe.

8.6 Behaviour you must not tolerate. Harassment, unwanted touching, sexual comments, threats, discrimination or being asked to do anything that makes you uncomfortable. Leave if you need to and tell us. We will support you and, where appropriate, stop sending cleaners to that customer.

8.7 Never put yourself at risk to protect property. Your safety comes first.

9. Our check-in procedure

9.1 We monitor check-ins during our operating hours (7am -8pm). If you do not check in within 30 minutes of the booking start time and we cannot reach you, we will:

• phone and message you;

• if there is no answer within 15 minutes, phone your emergency contact; and

• If there is still no answer and we are worried, ask the police to carry out a welfare check at the booking address.

9.2 If you cannot use the platform, tell us another way, by phone or email, and we will log it.

10. Reporting incidents

10.1 Report to us any of the following, however small:

• an injury or illness at work, or a near miss;

• a threat, harassment, abuse or assault, towards you or anyone else;

• damage to property or an allegation of theft;

• a safeguarding concern (section 6);

• a data incident, such as a lost key or access code, or personal information sent to the wrong person; and

• a vehicle accident or anything else that affected your work.

10.2 How and when. For anything urgent, call +44 7484 717935. Otherwise report through the platform or by email to hello@opulencebliss.com. Report immediately if someone is hurt or in danger, the same day for safeguarding concerns and threats, and within 24 hours for everything else.

10.3 What to tell us. What happened, when and where, who was involved, any injuries or damage, what you did, and whether anyone else saw it. Add photos if it is safe and appropriate.

10.4 What we do. We will contact you within 24 hours (the same day for serious incidents). We will check you are safe, offer support, record the incident, decide on any action, and tell you the outcome where we can. We may need to tell our insurer, the police, the local authority, the Health and Safety Executive (including under RIDDOR where it applies), or the ICO within 72 hours for a personal data breach.

10.5 We keep an incident log and review it at least every 6 months to find ways to make things safer.

11. Records, confidentiality and data protection

11.1 We keep safeguarding and incident records securely. Only the Safeguarding Lead and people who need them can see them. We share information only when we have to, to keep someone safe, or where the law requires or allows it. We do not promise absolute confidentiality when someone may be at risk.

11.2 We keep these records for 6 years, or longer where the law, a court or an authority requires. Records about a child are kept for longer where guidance says they should be.

11.3 We use this information under UK GDPR, relying on our legal duties, our legitimate interests in keeping people safe, and, where needed, the safeguarding conditions in Schedule 1 of the Data Protection Act 2018. See our Privacy Notice for more.

12. Training and review

12.1 Our onboarding team goes through this policy with every new cleaner and handyman, and you must confirm in writing (a tick box in the platform) that you have read it. We repeat a short refresher at least once a year.

12.2 We review this policy at least once a year and after any serious incident, or when the law changes.

13. Quick reference

• Immediate danger: call 999, then tell us.

• Worried about a customer: tell the Safeguarding Lead the same day. Write down facts. Do not investigate or promise secrecy.

• Feeling unsafe at a booking: leave and tell us. You will not be penalised.

• Running late or cannot check in: tell us.

• Any incident: report it within 24 hours, and the same day for threats or safeguarding.

14. Contact us

Opulence Bliss Ltd 128 City Road, London, United Kingdom, EC1V 2NX Company number: 15894675 Telephone: +44 7484 717935 Email: hello@opulencebliss.com

DBS AND CRIMINAL-OFFENCE DATA POLICY Appropriate Policy Document and Retention Schedule | Opulence Bliss Ltd | Version 1.0 | Effective from: 1 October 2026 This policy explains how we handle the results of basic Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) checks and any other information about criminal convictions. It is our "appropriate policy document" under Schedule 1 of the Data Protection Act 2018 and forms part of our data protection records.

1. Who we are and what this policy covers

1.1 Opulence Bliss Ltd ("we", "us"), company number 15894675, 128 City Road, London, United Kingdom, EC1V 2NX, is the controller of the personal information described here. We are registered with the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) under number ZC264981. Contact: hello@opulencebliss.com.

1.2 This policy covers the basic DBS certificates that cleaners and handymen show us before they take bookings, and any information about unspent criminal convictions that they or others tell us.

1.3 Information about criminal convictions is called "criminal offence data" under Article 10 of the UK GDPR. It needs extra protection.

2. What we process

2.1 We ask each cleaner and handyman to apply for their own basic DBS check at https://www.gov.uk/request-copy-criminal-record and show us the certificate. A basic check shows only unspent convictions and conditional cautions.

2.2 We record: the person's name, the certificate number and date, whether it showed nothing or showed an unspent conviction, a short note of the decision we made and why, and the date we reviewed it.

2.3 We may keep a copy of the certificate only for the short period set out in section 7. We do not ask for, or use, more information about convictions than we need.

3. Why we process it

3.1 Our cleaners and handymen work alone in customers' homes and businesses, sometimes with children, older people or other vulnerable people. We use DBS results to:

• protect customers, their property and the public;

• prevent and detect unlawful acts, such as theft, fraud and violence; and

• decide whether a person is suitable to work through our platform.

3.2 We use the information only for these purposes. We do not use it for marketing or any unrelated purpose.

4. Our legal basis

4.1 UK GDPR Article 6(1)(f), legitimate interests: our interest in keeping customers and our cleaners and handymen safe and preventing crime. We have balanced this against the privacy of the person checked.

4.2 Article 10 and Schedule 1 of the Data Protection Act 2018. We rely on these conditions for processing criminal offence data:

• Paragraph 10, preventing or detecting unlawful acts: where we need to carry out the check without the person's consent in order to prevent or detect unlawful acts, and asking for consent would prejudice that purpose; and

• Paragraph 11, protecting the public against dishonesty: where we need to decide whether a person is suitable to work in customers' homes.

4.3 We also ask the person to confirm that they agree that we may see and record their certificate. A person who does not agree cannot take bookings through the platform.

5. How we follow the data protection principles

5.1 Lawfulness, fairness and transparency. We tell every applicant, in our terms and privacy notice, that we ask for a DBS check, why, and how we handle the result. A decision is never based on a conviction alone (see section 6).

5.2 Purpose limitation. We use DBS information only for the purposes in section 3.

5.3 Data minimisation. We ask only for a basic check, we look at the certificate, we record only the details in section 2.2, and we do not keep a long-term copy.

5.4 Accuracy. The information comes directly from the person's own certificate. If they tell us something has changed, we update our record. We ask for a fresh certificate where we need to.

5.5 Storage limitation. We keep DBS information only for the periods in section 7, and then delete it securely.

5.6 Security. Certificates and records are kept in a restricted, access-controlled and encrypted location. Only the people named in section 8 can see them. We do not share them with customers or other cleaners or handymen, and we do not send them by ordinary email where we can avoid it.

5.7 Accountability. We keep a record of this processing, review this policy every 12 months, and keep a log of who has accessed DBS records.

6. How we make decisions

6.1 A conviction does not automatically stop someone working with us. We look at each case on its facts, including how serious and how relevant the offence is to the work, how long ago it was, what the person has done since, and the safety of customers.

6.2 We give the person the chance to explain before we make a decision, and we make it ourselves, not by an automated system.

6.3 We tell the person our decision in writing and explain it. They can ask us to review it.

6.4 We follow the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974. We do not ask about, or take into account, convictions that are spent, where the law says we must not.

7. Retention schedule

• Copy of the DBS certificate: we look at it and delete the copy within 6 months of the date we first saw it, unless we need it for a legal claim or investigation. It is then securely deleted.

• Record of the check (name, certificate number and date, outcome, decision note): kept while the person works with us, and for 6 months after their account closes. It is then securely deleted.

• Notes where we decided not to accept a person: kept for 6 months from our decision, in case the person challenges it. They are then securely deleted.

• Anything needed for a legal claim, regulator or police request: kept only for as long as that matter needs, then reviewed and deleted.

7.1 This policy is itself kept for at least 6 months after we stop processing this type of data, and is made available to the ICO on request.

8. Who can see it and who we share it with

8.1 Only the owner of the business and members of our onboarding team may see DBS information. The onboarding team carries out the checks. We authorise each team member in writing, keep a list of who they are, and tell each of them about this policy before they have access.

8.2 We do not share DBS information with customers, other cleaners or handymen, or businesses.

8.3 We share it only where the law requires or allows, for example with the police or another authority to prevent or detect crime, with a court, or with our insurers or advisers if needed for a claim. We do not sell it.

9. Your rights

9.1 You have the right to see your information, ask us to correct it, ask us to delete it, object to how we use it and ask us to restrict it, in line with UK data protection law. Some rights are limited where we must keep the information by law.

9.2 To use your rights, or if you are unhappy with how we handle your information, email hello@opulencebliss.com. We will acknowledge your complaint within 3 working days and reply without undue delay, and within 30 days in any case. You can also complain to the ICO at ico.org.uk or on 0303 123 1113.

10. Reviewing this policy

10.1 We review this policy at least once a year, and whenever our processing or the law changes. The current version is available to cleaners and handymen on request.

11. Contact us

Opulence Bliss Ltd 128 City Road, London, United Kingdom, EC1V 2NX Company number: 15894675 ICO registration number: ZC264981 Email: hello@opulencebliss.com
